	AppShellBreakpointXL:          "hidden xl:block",
}

// appshellMobileNavClasses show the MobileNav slot only below the breakpoint.
var appshellMobileNavClasses = map[AppShellBreakpoint]string{
	AppShellBreakpointUnspecified: "lg:hidden",
	AppShellBreakpointMD:          "md:hidden",
	AppShellBreakpointLG:          "lg:hidden",
	AppShellBreakpointXL:          "xl:hidden",
}

// appshellClassFor resolves a breakpoint-keyed class map, falling back to
// the default (zero-value) breakpoint entry.
func appshellClassFor(m map[AppShellBreakpoint]string, bp AppShellBreakpoint) string {
	return utils.Lookup(m, bp, m[AppShellBreakpointUnspecified])
}

// appshellContentColumnClass makes the content column a flex container so
// the (optional) header can be sticky while Content scrolls. flex-1 lets the
// column fill the shell's min-h-dvh below the grid breakpoint (above it the
// grid's align-items:stretch does the same), so the Footer slot's mt-auto
// pins to the true bottom at every viewport. min-w-0 is the flex-blowout
// guard (complements minmax(0,1fr) on the grid).
const appshellContentColumnClass = "flex flex-1 min-w-0 flex-col"

// AppShell renders a sidebar + header + content application shell. It is the
// 2D layout primitive for admin panels and dashboards: a fixed-width sidebar
// on desktop, an optional sticky header, and a flexible main area. Use it to
// replace the hand-rolled `grid lg:grid-cols-[16rem_1fr]` snippet every
// consumer rebuilds.
//
// AppShell renders INSIDE the `<main>` landmark provided by `layout.Base` —
// it does NOT emit its own `<main>` or skip-link (Base owns those, including
// the WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Block requirement).
//
//	@layout.Base(props) {
//	   @layout.AppShell(layout.AppShellProps{
//	      Sidebar:  navSidebar,
//	      Header:   navHeader,
//	      Content:  dashboardContent(),
//	   })
//	}
//
// # Mobile navigation
//
// The desktop Sidebar is hidden below the breakpoint — invisible on mobile.
// Pass a `display.Drawer` (or any mobile nav pattern) to MobileNav and AppShell
// will render it below the breakpoint only. This keeps layout free of the
// display import (respecting the import graph: layout → icons,utils only).
//
// # Grid-blowout safety
//
// The main column is `minmax(0, 1fr)` (not bare `1fr`). Without the `minmax`,
// a wide `<table>` or long URL in the content forces the column wider than
// the viewport, causing page-wide horizontal scroll. See ADR-0016 and the
// "minmax(0, 1fr) grid blowout footgun" recipe.
templ AppShell(props AppShellProps) {
	{{ sidebarW := sidebarWidthValue(props.SidebarWidth) }}
	<!-- Only shells WITH a sidebar consume the width token: a leftover
	     sidebar-width custom property on a sidebar-less shell misleads
	     consumer CSS (the two-track grid template is not emitted either;
	     see shellClassFor). -->
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class(shellClassFor(props.Sidebar, props.Breakpoint), props.Class) }
		if props.Sidebar != nil {
			style={ "--tc-sidebar-w: " + sidebarW }
		}
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Sidebar != nil {
			<div class={ appshellClassFor(appshellSidebarWrapperClasses, props.Breakpoint) }>
				@props.Sidebar
			</div>
		}
		if props.MobileNav != nil {
			<div class={ appshellClassFor(appshellMobileNavClasses, props.Breakpoint) }>
				@props.MobileNav
			</div>
		}
		<div class={ appshellContentColumnClass }>
			if props.Header != nil {
				<header
					class={ utils.Class(
						"border-b border-[var(--tc-header-border)] bg-[var(--tc-header-bg)]",
						utils.Ternary(props.StickyHeader, "sticky top-0 z-40", ""),
					) }
				>
					@props.Header
				</header>
			}
			<div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
				if props.Container && props.Content != nil {
					@Container(ContainerProps{
						BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{},
						Width:     props.ContainerWidth,
					}) {
						@props.Content
					}
				} else if props.Content != nil {
					@props.Content
				}
			</div>
			if props.Footer != nil {
				<footer class="mt-auto">
					@props.Footer
				</footer>
			}
		</div>
	</div>
}

# ── layout/appshell_types.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SidebarWidth is a typed enum for the desktop sidebar column width of an
// AppShell. Unknown values fall back to SidebarWidthMD.
type SidebarWidth string

const (
	// SidebarWidthSM is 12rem (w-48) — compact icon-heavy sidebars.
	SidebarWidthSM SidebarWidth = "sm"
	// SidebarWidthMD is 16rem (w-64) — the default, matches SidebarNav.
	SidebarWidthMD SidebarWidth = "md"
	// SidebarWidthLG is 20rem (w-80) — wide sidebars with labels + descriptions.
	SidebarWidthLG SidebarWidth = "lg"
	// SidebarWidthAuto sizes the sidebar to its content via `auto` in the grid
	// template. Use when the sidebar (e.g. SidebarNav) sets its own width and
	// the grid should not constrain it. CAUTION with SidebarNav specifically:
	// SidebarNav hardcodes `w-64` (16rem). Under SidebarWidthAuto the grid
	// track sizes to that element, which is fine — but under SidebarWidthSM
	// (12rem) the fixed `w-64` sidebar OVERFLOWS its 12rem track (the demo hit
	// this: it now uses the MD default). Either widen SidebarWidth, override
	// SidebarNav's width via its Class, or use Auto and let `w-64` win.
	SidebarWidthAuto SidebarWidth = "auto"
	// SidebarWidthDefault is the canonical default (MD).
	SidebarWidthDefault SidebarWidth = SidebarWidthMD
)

// SidebarWidthIsValid reports whether w is a recognized SidebarWidth.
func SidebarWidthIsValid(w SidebarWidth) bool {
	_, ok := sidebarWidthLookup[w]

	return ok
}

// sidebarWidthMD is the default sidebar width in CSS units. Extracted as a
// named constant to satisfy goconst (this value appears in the lookup table,
// the default fallback, and the godoc examples).
const sidebarWidthMDValue = "16rem"

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for sidebar widths
var sidebarWidthLookup = map[SidebarWidth]string{
	SidebarWidthSM:   "12rem",
	SidebarWidthMD:   sidebarWidthMDValue,
	SidebarWidthLG:   "20rem",
	SidebarWidthAuto: "auto",
}

// sidebarWidthValue returns the CSS grid-template-columns value (a length or
// "auto") for the sidebar column. Falls back to SidebarWidthDefault.
func sidebarWidthValue(w SidebarWidth) string {
	return utils.Lookup(sidebarWidthLookup, w, sidebarWidthLookup[SidebarWidthDefault])
}

// shellClassFor picks the AppShell outer wrapper class at the shell's
// hamburger breakpoint. The two-track grid template is only correct when a
// sidebar slot exists; with Sidebar nil the single content column would land
// in the sidebar-width track and collapse the shell, so the no-sidebar class
// is used instead.
func shellClassFor(sidebar templ.Component, bp AppShellBreakpoint) string {
	if sidebar == nil {
		return appshellShellNoSidebarClass
	}

	return appshellClassFor(appshellShellClasses, bp)
}

// AppShellProps configures a sidebar + content application shell. This is the
// 2D layout primitive every admin dashboard rebuilds by hand: a fixed-width
// sidebar on desktop, a sticky optional header, and a flexible main column.
//
// AppShell renders INSIDE the `<main>` landmark provided by `layout.Base` —
// it does NOT emit its own `<main>` or skip-link (Base owns those). Use it
// as the body content of Base:
//
//	@layout.Base(props) {
//	   @layout.AppShell(layout.AppShellProps{
//	      Sidebar:  navigation.SidebarNav(...),
//	      Header:   navigation.Nav(...),
//	      Content:  dashboardContent(),
//	   })
//	}
//
// # Mobile
//
// The desktop sidebar is `hidden lg:block` — invisible below the lg
// breakpoint. For mobile navigation, render a separate `display.Drawer` (or
// any other mobile pattern) and pass it as the MobileNav slot. AppShell will
// render that slot only below lg. This keeps layout free of the display
// import and gives the consumer full control over mobile UX.
//
// # Empty-slot contract
//
// Every slot is optional; nil renders predictably:
//
//	Sidebar    nil → no sidebar wrapper, NO --tc-sidebar-w style, single-column
//	             shell (the two-track grid is only emitted when a sidebar
//	             exists — emitting it anyway collapses the shell; fixed
//	             2026-09-08 after the dashboard recipe rendered ~16rem wide)
//	Header     nil → no <header> element
//	MobileNav  nil → nothing rendered below lg
//	Footer     nil → no <footer> element
//	Content    nil → empty content column (the shell frame still renders)
//
// # Embedded contexts and min-h-dvh
//
// The shell stretches to the full viewport height (`min-h-dvh`) because it
// is designed as the direct child of `layout.Base`'s <main>. When embedding
// an AppShell inside a card or other non-page container (like the demo
// does), override the height via Class: `utils.Class` merges consumer
// classes last, so `Class: "min-h-0"` (or an explicit height) wins over the
// shell default.
type AppShellProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Sidebar renders in the left grid column on desktop (lg+). Hidden on
	// mobile. Typically navigation.SidebarNav, but any templ.Component works.
	Sidebar templ.Component
	// MobileNav renders below lg only (lg:hidden). Optional. Use it to host a
	// display.Drawer or other mobile navigation pattern. Nil = no mobile nav.
	MobileNav templ.Component
	// Header renders inside the content column, sticky to the top when
	// StickyHeader is true. Typically navigation.Nav. Optional.
	Header templ.Component
	// Footer renders inside the content column, after Content, pinned to the
	// bottom of the viewport (mt-auto) at every breakpoint — the shell is a
	// full-height flex column below the grid breakpoint and a stretching grid
	// above it. Optional.
	Footer templ.Component
	// Content is the main body of the shell. Required.
	Content templ.Component
	// SidebarWidth controls the desktop sidebar column width via a CSS custom
	// property (--tc-sidebar-w). Default SidebarWidthMD (16rem). The main
	// column is always minmax(0, 1fr) — never bare 1fr (grid-blowout guard).
	SidebarWidth SidebarWidth
	// Breakpoint selects the viewport width at which the desktop sidebar
	// appears and the MobileNav hides — the hamburger breakpoint. Default
	// (zero value) keeps the historical lg: (1024px); md:/xl: cover
	// tablet-first and wide-dashboard shells (M22/F102).
	Breakpoint AppShellBreakpoint
	// StickyHeader pins the Header to the top of the content column on scroll.
	// Default true. Set to false for static headers.
	StickyHeader bool
	// Container, when true (default), wraps Content in a layout.Container at
	// ContainerWidth. Set to false when Content manages its own width
	// (e.g. an edge-to-edge table or map).
	Container bool
	// ContainerWidth is the max-width applied to the Content wrapper when
	// Container is true. Default ContainerWidthLG.
	ContainerWidth ContainerWidth
}

// AppShellBreakpoint is the viewport breakpoint at which AppShell switches
// from the mobile (single-column + MobileNav) to the desktop (sidebar grid)
// layout. The zero value resolves to AppShellBreakpointLG, the historical
// default.
type AppShellBreakpoint string

const (
	// AppShellBreakpointUnspecified is the zero value; it renders as lg.
	AppShellBreakpointUnspecified AppShellBreakpoint = ""
	// AppShellBreakpointMD shows the sidebar from 768px up.
	AppShellBreakpointMD AppShellBreakpoint = "md"
	// AppShellBreakpointLG shows the sidebar from 1024px up (the default).
	AppShellBreakpointLG AppShellBreakpoint = "lg"
	// AppShellBreakpointXL shows the sidebar from 1280px up.
	AppShellBreakpointXL AppShellBreakpoint = "xl"
)

// AppShellBreakpointIsValid reports whether b is a defined breakpoint (the
// zero value counts as defined: it means "use the default lg").
func AppShellBreakpointIsValid(b AppShellBreakpoint) bool {
	switch b {
	case AppShellBreakpointUnspecified, AppShellBreakpointMD, AppShellBreakpointLG, AppShellBreakpointXL:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// DefaultAppShellProps returns sensible defaults: MD sidebar, sticky header,
// Content wrapped in a Container at LG width.
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultAppShellProps() AppShellProps {
	return AppShellProps{
		SidebarWidth:   SidebarWidthDefault,
		StickyHeader:   true,
		Container:      true,
		ContainerWidth: ContainerWidthDefault,
	}
}

# ── layout/base.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "strings"

const (
	// DefaultThemeColor is the default light-mode theme color (indigo-600)
	DefaultThemeColor = "#4f46e5"
	// DefaultDarkThemeColor is the default dark-mode theme color (indigo-950)
	DefaultDarkThemeColor = "#1e1b4b"
)

// validHexColor reports whether s is a valid CSS hex color (#rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa).
func validHexColor(s string) bool {
	if len(s) < 4 || s[0] != '#' {
		return false
	}
	hex := s[1:]
	if len(hex) != 3 && len(hex) != 4 && len(hex) != 6 && len(hex) != 8 {
		return false
	}
	return strings.IndexFunc(hex, func(r rune) bool {
		return !strings.ContainsRune("0123456789abcdefABCDEF", r)
	}) == -1
}

// themeColor returns props.ThemeColor if valid, otherwise the default.
func themeColor(props PageProps) string {
	if validHexColor(props.ThemeColor) {
		return props.ThemeColor
	}
	return DefaultThemeColor
}

// darkThemeColor returns props.DarkThemeColor if valid, otherwise the default.
func darkThemeColor(props PageProps) string {
	if validHexColor(props.DarkThemeColor) {
		return props.DarkThemeColor
	}
	return DefaultDarkThemeColor
}

// resolveLocale returns locale if non-empty, otherwise the default "en".
// Used by Base and Minimal so the html lang attribute always has a valid value.
func resolveLocale(locale string) string {
	if locale == "" {
		return "en"
	}
	return locale
}

// ogType returns the Open Graph type, defaulting to "website" when empty.
func ogType(props PageProps) string {
	if props.OGType != "" {
		return props.OGType
	}
	return "website"
}

// skipLinkText returns the accessibility skip-link text, defaulting to
// "Skip to main content" when empty.
func skipLinkText(text string) string {
	if text != "" {
		return text
	}
	return "Skip to main content"
}

// SEOAlternate is one language-alternate URL for hreflang annotation. Lang
// is the hreflang tag ("en", "de", or "x-default"); URL must be absolute.
type SEOAlternate struct {
	Lang string
	URL  string
}

// SEOMeta carries the crawler/SEO head tags consumers otherwise hand-roll:
// robots noindex, canonical URL, hreflang alternates, and JSON-LD
// structured data. Empty fields emit nothing.
type SEOMeta struct {
	// NoIndex emits <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> for transient
	// pages (tailored variants, operator surfaces) that must stay out of
	// search results.
	NoIndex bool
	// Canonical emits <link rel="canonical">; empty omits the tag. Should
	// be an absolute URL.
	Canonical string
	// Alternates emits one <link rel="alternate" hreflang> per entry, in
	// order. Empty omits all.
	Alternates []SEOAlternate
	// JSONLD is embedded VERBATIM as <script type="application/ld+json">
	// via templ.Raw — it bypasses templ's auto-escaping by design. Only
	// pass trusted, correctly serialized JSON (marshal your struct with
	// encoding/json before handing it here); never interpolate user input.
	JSONLD string
}

// PageProps configures the base page layout
type PageProps struct {
	Title       string
	Description string
	Locale      string
	OGImage     string
	// OGType sets the Open Graph type for the og:type meta tag. Defaults to
	// "website" when empty. Common values: "website", "profile", "article".
	OGType         string
	ThemeColor     string
	DarkThemeColor string
	// CSSPath auto-injects `<link rel="stylesheet" href={CSSPath}>` into the
	// page `<head>`. DefaultPageProps sets it to "/app.css". Set CSSPath to ""
	// to suppress the stylesheet tag entirely — for example when you load
	// Tailwind via the browser Play CDN, embed styles inline, or serve your
	// own stylesheet through HeadContent.
	CSSPath string
	Favicon string
	// HTMXVersion controls auto-injection of the htmx `<script>` tag.
	// DefaultPageProps sets it to HTMXVersion2_0_10, which emits
	// `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/htmx.org@2.0.10" ...>`.
	// Set HTMXVersion to "" (the zero value) to disable auto-injection — for
	// example when you bundle htmx yourself, serve it from a local path via
	// HeadContent, or don't use htmx at all.
	HTMXVersion HTMXVersion
	// HTMXUseSRI adds an `integrity` attribute (subresource integrity) to the
	// auto-injected htmx script. Only meaningful when HTMXVersion is non-empty.
	HTMXUseSRI bool
	// HTMXCDN overrides the CDN base URL for htmx scripts. When empty, defaults
	// to "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm". Set to e.g. "https://unpkg.com" to use
	// a different CDN, or a self-hosted origin. Both the htmx main script and
	// the response-targets extension derive their URLs from this value.
	HTMXCDN string
	// HTMXNone renders NO htmx runtime at all: no script, no preconnect — for
	// pages that use no htmx-powered components (backlog #282). Components
	// degrade gracefully without the runtime.
	// HTMXSrc, when non-empty, switches the htmx main script from the CDN URL
	// to a self-hosted path. The value becomes the <script src> attribute verbatim.
	// Example: "/static/htmx.min.js". When set, HTMXVersion/HTMXCDN/HTMXUseSRI
	// are ignored for the main script (no SRI is emitted because the asset is
	// same-origin). The CDN response-targets extension is also suppressed — a
	// self-hoster manages extensions too. Add your own <script> tag for it if
	// needed. See ADR-0007.
	HTMXSrc string
	// HTMXResponseTargets controls whether the htmx response-targets extension
	// is loaded from the CDN alongside htmx. Defaults to true for backward
	// compatibility; set to false to skip the extra request. Ignored when
	// HTMXSrc is set (self-host implies you manage extensions).
	HTMXResponseTargets bool
	// SkipLinkText overrides the default "Skip to main content" text for the
	// accessibility skip link. Useful for i18n.
	SkipLinkText string
	// HTMLDataAttrs adds extra attributes to the <html> element (e.g.
	// data-nonce for Datastar's opt-in CSP mode, which reads root-level
	// attributes off document.documentElement). Keys are rendered as-is.
	// Pass nil for no extra attributes — the zero value keeps existing pages
	// byte-identical.
	HTMLDataAttrs templ.Attributes
	// BodyDataAttrs adds extra attributes to the <body> element (e.g.
	// data-language). Keys are rendered as-is. Pass nil for no extra attributes.
	BodyDataAttrs templ.Attributes
	BodyClass     string
	Nonce         string
	// SEO carries crawler/SEO head tags (noindex, canonical, hreflang
	// alternates, JSON-LD). Zero value emits nothing — existing pages keep
	// byte-identical output.
	SEO         SEOMeta
	HeadContent templ.Component
	Footer      templ.Component
	// SecurityHeaders is a deprecated no-op: HTTP security headers cannot be
	// expressed as meta tags (browsers ignore meta http-equiv for
	// X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy, and the latter was never a
	// registered http-equiv, so the emitted tags were invalid HTML that
	// failed HTML validation). Send real headers at the server instead. The
	// field remains for API compatibility and emits nothing.
	SecurityHeaders bool
	// NoMainWrapper, when true, omits the `<main id="main-content">` wrapper
	// and renders children directly under <body> — for pages whose content is
	// itself a full landmark component (errorpage.ErrorPage and
	// errorpage.NotFound404 render their own <main>; nesting a second <main>
	// is an HTML violation and an axe/html-validate failure). The skip link
	// still targets #main-content, so give your own landmark that ID
	// (errorpage.NotFound404Props.BaseProps.ID accepts it, plus a tabindex
	// Attr for skip-link focus). Zero value keeps the wrapper — existing
	// pages render byte-identically.
	NoMainWrapper bool
	// NoThemeScript, when true, skips the inline dark-mode preload script
	// Base emits in <head> (the ThemeScript that reads localStorage['theme']
	// and sets the .dark class + color-scheme before paint). For consumers
	// running a strict CSP that allows no inline scripts: ship the same
	// logic as a same-origin, render-blocking <script src> via HeadContent,
	// or drop the script entirely when the page only follows
	// prefers-color-scheme (the script is only needed for the toggle dark
	// strategy — see ThemeScript's doc). Zero value keeps the script —
	// existing pages render byte-identically.
	NoThemeScript bool
}

// DefaultPageProps returns sensible defaults for PageProps.
//
// Two fields auto-inject `<head>` tags and are the most common defaults to
// override when integrating with an existing asset pipeline:
//
//   - CSSPath ("/app.css") — set to "" if you serve styles another way.
//   - HTMXVersion (HTMXVersion2_0_10) — set to "" to suppress the htmx CDN tag.
//
// HTMXResponseTargets defaults to true (loads the response-targets extension
// alongside htmx); set to false to skip the extra request when unused.
func DefaultPageProps() PageProps {
	return PageProps{
		Locale:              "en",
		OGType:              "website",
		SkipLinkText:        "Skip to main content",
		ThemeColor:          DefaultThemeColor,
		DarkThemeColor:      DefaultDarkThemeColor,
		CSSPath:             "/app.css",
		Favicon:             "/favicon.svg",
		HTMXVersion:         HTMXVersion2_0_10,
		HTMXSrc:             HTMXSelfHost,
		HTMXUseSRI:          true,
		HTMXResponseTargets: true,
		SecurityHeaders:     true,
		BodyClass:           "bg-white text-gray-900 antialiased min-h-dvh flex flex-col scroll-smooth motion-reduce:scroll-auto selection:bg-blue-100 dark:selection:bg-blue-900 selection:text-blue-900 dark:selection:text-blue-100 dark:bg-gray-950 dark:text-gray-100",
	}
}

// Base renders a complete HTML5 base layout with HTMX, theme support, and meta tags
// Use with children... to inject page content into the body
//
//	@layout.Base(props) {
//	  <h1>My Page</h1>
//	}
templ Base(props PageProps) {
	{{ locale := resolveLocale(props.Locale) }}
	<!DOCTYPE html>
	<html lang={ locale } class="h-full" { props.HTMLDataAttrs... }>
		<head>
			<meta charset="UTF-8"/>
			<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"/>
			<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"/>
			<title>{ props.Title }</title>
			if props.Description != "" {
				<meta name="description" content={ props.Description }/>
			}
			if props.SEO.NoIndex || props.SEO.Canonical != "" || len(props.SEO.Alternates) > 0 || props.SEO.JSONLD != "" {
				@seoHeadTags(props.SEO)
			}
			if props.Favicon != "" {
				<link rel="icon" href={ props.Favicon }/>
			}
			<meta name="theme-color" content={ themeColor(props) } media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"/>
			<meta name="theme-color" content={ darkThemeColor(props) } media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"/>
			<meta property="og:title" content={ props.Title }/>
			if props.Description != "" {
				<meta property="og:description" content={ props.Description }/>
			}
			<meta property="og:type" content={ ogType(props) }/>
			if props.OGImage != "" {
				<meta property="og:image" content={ props.OGImage }/>
			}
			if props.Locale != "" {
				<meta property="og:locale" content={ props.Locale }/>
			}
			if props.OGImage != "" {
				<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image"/>
			} else {
				<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary"/>
			}
			<meta name="twitter:title" content={ props.Title }/>
			if props.Description != "" {
				<meta name="twitter:description" content={ props.Description }/>
			}
			if props.OGImage != "" {
				<meta name="twitter:image" content={ props.OGImage }/>
			}
			if !props.NoThemeScript {
				@ThemeScript(props.Nonce)
			}
			if props.CSSPath != "" {
				<link rel="stylesheet" href={ props.CSSPath }/>
			}
			if props.HTMXSrc != HTMXNone && (props.HTMXVersion != "" || props.HTMXSrc != "") {
				{{ cdnOrigin := htmxCDNOrigin(props.HTMXCDN) }}
				if cdnOrigin != "" && props.HTMXSrc == "" {
					<link rel="preconnect" href={ cdnOrigin } crossorigin/>
					<link rel="dns-prefetch" href={ cdnOrigin }/>
				}
				if props.HTMXSrc == HTMXSelfHost {
					@htmxSelfHostComponent(props.Nonce)
				} else if props.HTMXSrc != "" {
					<script src={ props.HTMXSrc }></script>
				} else if props.HTMXUseSRI {
					{{ mainSRI := htmxMainSRI(props.HTMXVersion) }}
					if mainSRI != "" {
						<script src={ htmxScriptURL(props.HTMXVersion, props.HTMXCDN) } integrity={ mainSRI } crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
					} else {
						<script src={ htmxScriptURL(props.HTMXVersion, props.HTMXCDN) }></script>
					}
				} else {
					<script src={ htmxScriptURL(props.HTMXVersion, props.HTMXCDN) }></script>
				}
				if props.HTMXResponseTargets && props.HTMXSrc == "" {
					if props.HTMXUseSRI {
						<script src={ responseTargetsURL(props.HTMXCDN) } integrity={ sriResponseTargets } crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
					} else {
						<script src={ responseTargetsURL(props.HTMXCDN) }></script>
					}
				}
			}
			if props.HeadContent != nil {
				@props.HeadContent
			}
		</head>
		<body class={ props.BodyClass } { props.BodyDataAttrs... }>
			<a href="#main-content" class="sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:absolute focus:top-2 focus:start-2 focus:z-50 focus:bg-blue-600 dark:focus:bg-blue-500 focus:text-white focus:px-4 focus:py-2 focus:rounded-md focus:shadow-lg focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-offset-2 dark:focus:ring-offset-gray-900 focus:ring-blue-500 dark:focus:ring-blue-400">
				{ skipLinkText(props.SkipLinkText) }
			</a>
			if props.NoMainWrapper {
				{ children... }
			} else {
				<main id="main-content" tabindex="-1" class="flex-1">
					{ children... }
				</main>
			}
			if props.Footer != nil {
				@props.Footer
			}
		</body>
	</html>
}

// MinimalProps configures a minimal HTML5 document without HTMX or external dependencies
type MinimalProps struct {
	Title  string
	Locale string
	// SEO optionally emits the crawler/SEO head tags (robots noindex,
	// canonical, hreflang alternates, JSON-LD) with the same semantics as
	// PageProps.SEO. Zero value emits nothing — Minimal stays
	// dependency-free unless a tag is explicitly requested.
	SEO SEOMeta
	// HeadContent, when set, renders verbatim into <head> after the SEO
	// tags — the Minimal twin of PageProps.HeadContent: critical inline
	// styles, fonts, or extra meta tags without graduating to Base.
	HeadContent templ.Component
}

// DefaultMinimalProps returns sensible defaults for MinimalProps
func DefaultMinimalProps() MinimalProps {
	return MinimalProps{
		Locale: "en",
	}
}

// Minimal renders a minimal HTML5 document without HTMX or external dependencies.
// Defaults Locale to "en" when empty (valid HTML lang attribute).
// Useful for static pages, emails, or PDF generation
//
//	@layout.Minimal(layout.MinimalProps{Title: "My Title"}) {
//	  <h1>Hello</h1>
//	}
templ Minimal(props MinimalProps) {
	{{ locale := resolveLocale(props.Locale) }}
	<!DOCTYPE html>
	<html lang={ locale }>
		<head>
			<meta charset="UTF-8"/>
			<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"/>
			<title>{ props.Title }</title>
			@seoHeadTags(props.SEO)
			if props.HeadContent != nil {
				@props.HeadContent
			}
		</head>
		<body>
			{ children... }
		</body>
	</html>
}

// seoHeadTags renders the crawler/SEO head tags shared by Base and Minimal:
// robots noindex, canonical URL, hreflang alternates, and JSON-LD. Empty
// fields emit nothing, so callers can always pass the struct through.
templ seoHeadTags(seo SEOMeta) {
	if seo.NoIndex {
		<meta name="robots" content="noindex"/>
	}
	if seo.Canonical != "" {
		<link rel="canonical" href={ seo.Canonical }/>
	}
	for _, alt := range seo.Alternates {
		<link rel="alternate" hreflang={ alt.Lang } href={ alt.URL }/>
	}
	if seo.JSONLD != "" {
		@templ.Raw("<script type=\"application/ld+json\">" + seo.JSONLD + "</script>")
	}
}

# ── layout/container.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// containerPadClass is the responsive horizontal padding applied by Container
// unless NoPad is set. Matches the convention used across the demo and is the
// single source of truth for "page gutter" width.
const containerPadClass = "px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8"

// Container renders a centered max-width wrapper with responsive horizontal
// padding. Use it as the single source of truth for page content width and
// page gutter — replacing the hand-rolled
// `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8` snippet repeated in every consumer.
//
// # Defaults
//
// Width=ContainerWidthLG (max-w-7xl). The responsive gutter (px-4 sm:px-6
// lg:px-8) is on by DEFAULT — including in a bare `ContainerProps{...}`
// struct literal, where the zero value is the padded common case. Set
// `NoPad: true` only for edge-to-edge content (maps, full-bleed tables) where
// the consumer manages padding. (Historical note: before NoPad existed, the
// flag was `Pad bool` with a documented default of true that struct literals
// silently violated — every literal had to remember `Pad: true` or lost the
// gutter. NoPad restores the Go idiom that the zero value is the default.)
//
// # Examples
//
// Default dashboard width:
//
//	@layout.Container(layout.DefaultContainerProps()) {
//	   @display.Grid(display.DefaultGridProps()) { ... }
//	}
//
// Long-form article:
//
//	@layout.Container(layout.ContainerProps{Width: layout.ContainerWidthProse}) {
//	   { articleBody }
//	}
//
// Edge-to-edge map or chart (consumer manages padding):
//
//	@layout.Container(layout.ContainerProps{Width: layout.ContainerWidthFull, NoPad: true}) {
//	   { mapComponent }
//	}
templ Container(props ContainerProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class(
			"mx-auto w-full " + containerWidthClass(props.Width),
			utils.Ternary(props.NoPad, "", containerPadClass),
			props.Class,
		) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ children... }
	</div>
}

# ── layout/container_types.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// ContainerWidth is a typed enum for the maximum width of a Container. Unknown
// values fall back to ContainerWidthLG (graceful degradation — never panic).
type ContainerWidth string

const (
	// ContainerWidthSM narrows the container to max-w-3xl (48rem) — for
	// sign-in forms, focused single-purpose pages, and short articles.
	ContainerWidthSM ContainerWidth = "sm"
	// ContainerWidthMD is max-w-5xl (64rem) — for two-column layouts and
	// medium-density pages.
	ContainerWidthMD ContainerWidth = "md"
	// ContainerWidthLG is max-w-7xl (80rem) — the application default for
	// dashboards, list pages, and admin panels.
	ContainerWidthLG ContainerWidth = "lg"
	// ContainerWidthXL is max-w-[90rem] — for wide dashboards and data-heavy
	// layouts that need more horizontal real estate than LG.
	ContainerWidthXL ContainerWidth = "xl"
	// ContainerWidthFull is max-w-full — full-bleed edge-to-edge content.
	// Pair with explicit px-* padding on the consumer side.
	ContainerWidthFull ContainerWidth = "full"
	// ContainerWidthProse is max-w-prose (65ch) — for long-form articles and
	// documentation where line length must stay readable.
	ContainerWidthProse ContainerWidth = "prose"
	// ContainerWidthDefault is the canonical default (LG).
	ContainerWidthDefault ContainerWidth = ContainerWidthLG
)

// ContainerWidthIsValid reports whether w is a recognized ContainerWidth.
func ContainerWidthIsValid(w ContainerWidth) bool {
	_, ok := containerWidthLookup[w]

	return ok
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for container widths
var containerWidthLookup = map[ContainerWidth]string{
	ContainerWidthSM:    "max-w-3xl",
	ContainerWidthMD:    "max-w-5xl",
	ContainerWidthLG:    "max-w-7xl",
	ContainerWidthXL:    "max-w-[90rem]",
	ContainerWidthFull:  "max-w-full",
	ContainerWidthProse: "max-w-prose",
}

// containerWidthClass returns the Tailwind max-width class for a width, with
// fallback to ContainerWidthDefault for unknown values (map+fallback pattern).
func containerWidthClass(w ContainerWidth) string {
	return utils.Lookup(containerWidthLookup, w, containerWidthLookup[ContainerWidthDefault])
}

// ContainerProps configures a content Container — a centered max-width wrapper
// with responsive horizontal padding. This is the single source of truth for
// page content width; use it to replace the repeated
// `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8` snippet.
//
// All new page content should be wrapped in a Container. AppShell already
// wraps its main content slot in a Container by default — set AppShellProps
// .Container=false to opt out (e.g. when the page itself manages width).
type ContainerProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Width controls the max-width. Default is ContainerWidthLG.
	// Use ContainerWidthProse for long-form articles.
	Width ContainerWidth
	// NoPad suppresses the responsive horizontal gutter
	// (px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8). The gutter is ON by default — the zero
	// value is the padded common case, so struct literals keep it
	// without setting anything. Set NoPad to true only when the
	// consumer manages padding (e.g. edge-to-edge maps inside a
	// ContainerWidthFull wrapper, or nesting inside a Card/Grid).
	NoPad bool
}

// DefaultContainerProps returns sensible defaults: LG width. The responsive
// gutter needs no explicit opt-in — it is the zero-value default.
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultContainerProps() ContainerProps {
	return ContainerProps{
		Width: ContainerWidthDefault,
	}
}

# ── layout/doc.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// Package layout provides page-level layout components including base HTML shell,
// containers, and structural templates.
package layout

# ── layout/embed.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import (
	"context"
	_ "embed"
	"fmt"
	"html"
	"io"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

//go:embed static/htmx.min.js
var htmxSource string

// HTMXSelfHost is the sentinel value for PageProps.HTMXSrc that triggers
// inline embedding of the HTMX source (v2.0 default). When HTMXSrc is set
// to HTMXSelfHost, the HTMX script is rendered inline via a <script> tag
// with the embedded source, avoiding any external CDN request.
const HTMXSelfHost = "self"

// HTMXNone is the sentinel value for PageProps.HTMXSrc that renders NO htmx
// runtime at all (backlog #282). Choose it when a page uses no htmx-powered
// components (or wires everything through Datastar): Base then emits no
// htmx <script>, no CDN preconnect/dns-prefetch hints, and no SRI — smaller
// pages, zero framework bytes. Every library component degrades gracefully
// without the runtime: wired anchors/forms fall back to plain navigation or
// no-op, and unwired markup is unaffected.
const HTMXNone = "none"

// htmxSelfHostComponent returns a templ.Component that renders the embedded
// HTMX source inline in a nonce-protected <script> tag. Used when
// PageProps.HTMXSrc == HTMXSelfHost. Writing raw HTML via ComponentFunc is
// required because templ's <script> context sanitizes interpolation. An
// empty nonce omits the attribute entirely (nonce="" is rejected by
// strict-CSP pages — the omit-empty rule, see utils.ScriptAttrs).
func htmxSelfHostComponent(nonce string) templ.Component {
	nonceAttr := ""
	if nonce != "" {
		nonceAttr = fmt.Sprintf(" nonce=\"%s\"", html.EscapeString(nonce))
	}

	return templ.ComponentFunc(func(_ context.Context, w io.Writer) error {
		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, `<script%s>%s</script>`, nonceAttr, htmxSource)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("write inline htmx script: %w", err)
		}

		return nil
	})
}

# ── layout/meta_refresh.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "strconv"

// MetaRefresh renders a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` tag that reloads or
// redirects the page without JavaScript — the zero-JS retry/stale-session
// pattern (dnsblockd's login guard and allow-list retry pages both use it).
//
// With url empty the page reloads itself after delay seconds; otherwise the
// browser navigates to url. Negative delays clamp to 0 (immediate).
//
//	@layout.MetaRefresh(5, "/login?retry=1")
//	@layout.MetaRefresh(30, "") // reload this page every 30s
templ MetaRefresh(delaySeconds int, url string) {
	{{
		refreshContent := strconv.Itoa(max(delaySeconds, 0))
		if url != "" {
			refreshContent += ";url=" + url
		}
	}}
	<meta http-equiv="refresh" content={ refreshContent }/>
}

# ── layout/script.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

// Script renders a CSP-safe external `<script src="...">` tag with the nonce
// applied automatically. Use it instead of a raw `<script>` tag so the nonce
// can never be forgotten — under a strict Content-Security-Policy a forgotten
// nonce silently breaks the script in the browser with no error in your logs.
//
// Pass optional attributes (async, defer, type="module", crossorigin, …) via
// attrs. Do not pass `nonce` via attrs; the nonce parameter owns it.
//
//	@layout.Script(nonce, "/static/app.js", nil)
//	@layout.Script(nonce, "/static/app.js", templ.Attributes{"defer": true})
//	@layout.Script(nonce, "/static/tailwind.min.js", templ.Attributes{"type": "module"})
templ Script(nonce string, src string, attrs templ.Attributes) {
	<script src={ src } nonce={ nonce } { attrs... }></script>
}

# ── layout/split.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// Lookup maps live in this .templ file (not split_types.go) so Tailwind's
// content scanner detects the class strings — it only scans *.templ files.

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for split ratios
var splitRatioLookup = map[SplitRatio]string{
	SplitRatio1To2: "md:grid-cols-2",
	SplitRatio1To3: "md:grid-cols-3",
	SplitRatio1To4: "md:grid-cols-4",
}

// splitRatioLookupContainer mirrors splitRatioLookup with @container-keyed
// breakpoints (@md:) so container-aware Splits respond to their parent's
// width instead of the viewport. See ADR-0018.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for container-aware variant
var splitRatioLookupContainer = map[SplitRatio]string{
	SplitRatio1To2: "@md:grid-cols-2",
	SplitRatio1To3: "@md:grid-cols-3",
	SplitRatio1To4: "@md:grid-cols-4",
}

// splitRatioCols returns the grid-template-columns class for a ratio.
func splitRatioCols(r SplitRatio, containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return utils.Lookup(splitRatioLookupContainer, r, splitRatioLookupContainer[SplitRatioDefault])
	}

	return utils.Lookup(splitRatioLookup, r, splitRatioLookup[SplitRatioDefault])
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table
var splitRatioMainSpanLookup = map[SplitRatio]string{
	SplitRatio1To2: "md:col-span-1",
	SplitRatio1To3: "md:col-span-2",
	SplitRatio1To4: "md:col-span-3",
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table
var splitRatioMainSpanLookupContainer = map[SplitRatio]string{
	SplitRatio1To2: "@md:col-span-1",
	SplitRatio1To3: "@md:col-span-2",
	SplitRatio1To4: "@md:col-span-3",
}

// splitRatioMainSpan returns the col-span-N class for the Main column.
func splitRatioMainSpan(r SplitRatio, containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return utils.Lookup(splitRatioMainSpanLookupContainer, r, splitRatioMainSpanLookupContainer[SplitRatio1To3])
	}

	return utils.Lookup(splitRatioMainSpanLookup, r, splitRatioMainSpanLookup[SplitRatio1To3])
}

// splitAsideSpan returns the col-span-1 class for the Aside column.
func splitAsideSpan(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "@md:col-span-1"
	}

	return "md:col-span-1"
}

// Split renders a 2-column main + aside layout. It is the second most common
// 2D pattern after AppShell: article+sidebar, detail+metadata, primary
// content + related links.
//
// Both columns use minmax(0,1fr) per grid track to prevent grid blowout
// (see ADR-0016). The layout stacks to a single column below md (mobile).
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the 2-column collapse respond to the
// parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the viewport. Useful
// when Split is placed inside a sidebar, card body, drawer, or other
// constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
//
// # RTL / logical ordering
//
// AsidePosition uses logical (Start/End) names, not physical (Left/Right).
// In LTR: Start=left, End=right. In RTL (dir="rtl"): Start=right, End=left.
// Source order + CSS grid auto-placement handles the mirror — no physical
// left/right utilities are emitted.
//
//	@layout.Split(layout.SplitProps{
//	   Main:   articleBody,
//	   Aside:  tocWidget,
//	   Ratio:  layout.SplitRatio1To3,
//	})
templ Split(props SplitProps) {
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@splitInner(props)
		</div>
	} else {
		@splitInner(props)
	}
}

templ splitInner(props SplitProps) {
	{{ gap := props.Gap }}
	if gap == "" {
		{{ gap = "gap-6" }}
	}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class(
			"grid grid-cols-1",
			splitRatioCols(props.Ratio, props.ContainerAware),
			gap,
			props.Class,
		) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.AsidePosition == AsidePositionStart && props.Aside != nil {
			<aside class={ utils.Class(splitAsideSpan(props.ContainerAware), "min-w-0") }>
				@props.Aside
			</aside>
		}
		if props.Main != nil {
			<div class={ utils.Class("min-w-0", splitRatioMainSpan(props.Ratio, props.ContainerAware)) }>
				@props.Main
			</div>
		}
		if props.AsidePosition != AsidePositionStart && props.Aside != nil {
			<aside class={ utils.Class(splitAsideSpan(props.ContainerAware), "min-w-0") }>
				@props.Aside
			</aside>
		}
	</div>
}

# ── layout/split_types.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// Lookup maps and helper functions live in split.templ (not this file) so
// Tailwind's content scanner can detect the class strings — it only scans
// *.templ files, not *.go files. See Grid, Card, Nav for the same pattern.

// SplitRatio is a typed enum for the relative widths of the Main and Aside
// columns in a Split. Unknown values fall back to SplitRatio1To3.
type SplitRatio string

const (
	// SplitRatio1To3 — Main takes 2/3, Aside takes 1/3 (default, classic
	// article+sidebar pattern).
	SplitRatio1To3 SplitRatio = "1-3"
	// SplitRatio1To4 — Main takes 3/4, Aside takes 1/4 (wide main, narrow aside).
	SplitRatio1To4 SplitRatio = "1-4"
	// SplitRatio1To2 — Main and Aside are equal width.
	SplitRatio1To2 SplitRatio = "1-2"
	// SplitRatioDefault is the canonical default (1To3).
	SplitRatioDefault SplitRatio = SplitRatio1To3
)

// SplitRatioIsValid reports whether r is a recognized SplitRatio.
func SplitRatioIsValid(r SplitRatio) bool {
	return r == SplitRatio1To2 || r == SplitRatio1To3 || r == SplitRatio1To4
}

// AsidePosition controls whether the Aside renders before (start) or after
// (end) the Main content. Both are logical positions — they auto-mirror in
// RTL contexts because the grid uses source order, not physical left/right.
type AsidePosition string

const (
	// AsidePositionEnd renders Aside AFTER Main (default — sidebar on the
	// right in LTR, left in RTL).
	AsidePositionEnd AsidePosition = "end"
	// AsidePositionStart renders Aside BEFORE Main (sidebar on the left in
	// LTR, right in RTL).
	AsidePositionStart AsidePosition = "start"
	// AsidePositionDefault is the canonical default (End).
	AsidePositionDefault AsidePosition = AsidePositionEnd
)

// AsidePositionIsValid reports whether p is a recognized AsidePosition.
func AsidePositionIsValid(p AsidePosition) bool {
	return p == AsidePositionStart || p == AsidePositionEnd
}

// SplitProps configures a 2-column content + aside layout — the second most
// common 2D pattern after AppShell. Use it for article+sidebar widgets,
// detail+metadata, or any main-content-with-secondary-content layout.
//
// Both columns use minmax(0,1fr) per grid track to prevent grid blowout
// from wide content (see ADR-0016). The layout collapses to a single
// stacked column below the md breakpoint (mobile-friendly by default).
type SplitProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Main is the primary content column. Required.
	Main templ.Component
	// Aside is the secondary content column (sidebar, metadata, related
	// links). Required.
	Aside templ.Component
	// AsidePosition controls whether Aside renders before or after Main.
	// Default AsidePositionEnd (aside after main in source order + visual).
	AsidePosition AsidePosition
	// Ratio controls the relative column widths. Default SplitRatio1To3
	// (main 2/3, aside 1/3).
	Ratio SplitRatio
	// Gap controls spacing between the two columns. Default GridGapLG (1.5rem).
	Gap string
	// ContainerAware, when true, wraps the Split in a @container div and swaps
	// md: breakpoint classes for @md: so the 2-column collapse responds to the
	// parent container's width, not the viewport. Useful when Split is placed
	// inside a sidebar, card body, drawer, or other constrained layout. Default
	// false (viewport breakpoints). See ADR-0018.
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultSplitProps returns sensible defaults: aside at end, 1To3 ratio, gap-6.
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultSplitProps() SplitProps {
	return SplitProps{
		AsidePosition:  AsidePositionDefault,
		Ratio:          SplitRatioDefault,
		Gap:            "gap-6",
		ContainerAware: true,
	}
}

# ── layout/sri.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// HTMX CDN version pinning and SRI hash lookup.
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/cdn"

// HTMXVersion is a pinned HTMX main-script version. Use the exported constants
// (e.g. HTMXVersion2_0_10) for compile-time safety; custom versions can be
// constructed via HTMXVersion("x.y.z") but will render without SRI (no integrity hash).
type HTMXVersion string

const (
	// HTMXVersion2_0_10 is the htmx main-script version DefaultPageProps pins.
	HTMXVersion2_0_10 HTMXVersion = "2.0.10"

	// defaultHTMXVersion is the internal default; always equals the latest
	// exported HTMXVersion constant.
	defaultHTMXVersion HTMXVersion = HTMXVersion2_0_10
)

// HTMX 2.x split its extensions into standalone pnpm packages with independent
// version numbers. The response-targets extension is no longer bundled inside
// the htmx.org package: loading htmx.org@<v>/dist/ext/response-targets.js
// emits the console warning "You are using an htmx 1 extension with htmx 2.0.x"
// because that file is the legacy htmx 1 build. The v2-compatible build ships
// as the separate package htmx-ext-response-targets, pinned below.
const (
	// responseTargetsVersion is the pinned version of the separate
	// htmx-ext-response-targets package. It is independent of defaultHTMXVersion.
	responseTargetsVersion = "2.0.4"
)

// defaultCDNBase is the CDN base URL used when PageProps.HTMXCDN is empty.
// Both htmx.org and htmx-ext-response-targets are served from pnpm-style paths
// under this base. Consumers override via PageProps.HTMXCDN (e.g.
// "https://unpkg.com" or a self-hosted origin).
const defaultCDNBase = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm"

// sriResponseTargets is the sha384 (base64) SRI hash for the pinned
// response-targets extension build.
const sriResponseTargets = "sha384-T41oglUPvXLGBVyRdZsVRxNWnOOqCynaPubjUVjxhsjFTKrFJGEMm3/0KGmNQ+Pg"

// sriHTMXMainByVersion maps an htmx main-script version to its SRI hash.
// Only versions listed here render an integrity attribute; a caller who pins a
// different version via PageProps.HTMXVersion gets the script without SRI.
//
// Regenerate a hash after a bump with:
//
//	curl -sL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/htmx.org@<v> | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A
//
// sriHTMXMainDefault is the sha384 SRI hash for the pinned default htmx version.
const sriHTMXMainDefault = "sha384-H5SrcfygHmAuTDZphMHqBJLc3FhssKjG7w/CeCpFReSfwBWDTKpkzPP8c+cLsK+V"

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Version-keyed SRI lookup table.
var sriHTMXMainByVersion = map[HTMXVersion]string{
	HTMXVersion2_0_10: sriHTMXMainDefault,
}

// resolveCDNBase returns cdnBase if non-empty, otherwise defaultCDNBase.
// A trailing slash is trimmed so consumers can pass "https://unpkg.com/" safely.
func resolveCDNBase(cdnBase string) string {
	return cdn.ResolveBase(cdnBase, defaultCDNBase)
}

// htmxCDNOrigin extracts the scheme+host (origin) from the CDN base URL for
// use in <link rel="preconnect">. Returns "" if the input doesn't parse as
// an absolute URL (e.g. a relative self-hosted path like "/assets").
func htmxCDNOrigin(cdnBase string) string {
	return cdn.Origin(cdnBase, defaultCDNBase)
}

// htmxScriptURL returns the CDN URL for the htmx main script at the given
// version. If cdnBase is empty, defaults to defaultCDNBase.
func htmxScriptURL(version HTMXVersion, cdnBase string) string {
	return resolveCDNBase(cdnBase) + "/htmx.org@" + string(version)
}

// responseTargetsURL returns the CDN URL for the response-targets extension.
// If cdnBase is empty, defaults to defaultCDNBase.
func responseTargetsURL(cdnBase string) string {
	return resolveCDNBase(cdnBase) + "/htmx-ext-response-targets@" +
		responseTargetsVersion + "/dist/response-targets.min.js"
}

// htmxMainSRI returns the SRI hash for the htmx main script at the given
// version. Returns empty string for unpinned versions — the browser will
// load the script without SRI verification, which is safer than returning
// a wrong hash (the browser would block the script on hash mismatch).
func htmxMainSRI(version HTMXVersion) string {
	return sriHTMXMainByVersion[version]
}

# ── layout/stack.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// Stack renders a vertical flex container with typed gap spacing. It is the
// single source of truth for vertical rhythm — replacing the repeated
// `space-y-4` / `space-y-6` strings scattered across consumer pages.
//
// Stack is the 1D vertical counterpart to Grid. Use Stack when only the
// vertical axis matters (a column of cards, a list of form fields, a stack
// of alerts). Use Grid when both rows AND columns matter (card dashboards,
// multi-column layouts). See ADR-0016.
//
//	@layout.Stack(layout.DefaultStackProps()) {
//	   @display.Card(...)
//	   @display.Card(...)
//	}
templ Stack(props StackProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("flex flex-col", stackGapClass(props.Gap), props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ children... }
	</div>
}

# ── layout/stack_types.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// StackGap is a typed enum for vertical spacing between stacked children.
// Unknown values fall back to StackGapMD. Mirrors the GridGap shape so the
// two composition primitives share a vocabulary.
type StackGap string

const (
	StackGapNone StackGap = "none"
	StackGapSM   StackGap = "sm" // space-y-2 (0.5rem)
	StackGapMD   StackGap = "md" // space-y-4 (1rem) — default
	StackGapLG   StackGap = "lg" // space-y-6 (1.5rem)
	StackGapXL   StackGap = "xl" // space-y-8 (2rem)
	// StackGapDefault is the canonical default (MD).
	StackGapDefault StackGap = StackGapMD
)

// StackGapIsValid reports whether g is a recognized StackGap.
func StackGapIsValid(g StackGap) bool {
	_, ok := stackGapLookup[g]

	return ok
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for stack gaps
var stackGapLookup = map[StackGap]string{
	StackGapNone: "",
	StackGapSM:   "space-y-2",
	StackGapMD:   "space-y-4",
	StackGapLG:   "space-y-6",
	StackGapXL:   "space-y-8",
}

// stackGapClass returns the Tailwind space-y-* class for a gap. Empty string
// for None. Falls back to StackGapDefault for unknown values.
func stackGapClass(g StackGap) string {
	return utils.Lookup(stackGapLookup, g, stackGapLookup[StackGapDefault])
}

// StackProps configures a vertical stack of children with consistent spacing.
// Use Stack to replace repeated `space-y-N` strings — it is the 1D vertical
// counterpart to the 2D Grid primitive. Stack is flex-col (NOT grid): both
// axes do not matter, only the vertical rhythm. See ADR-0016.
type StackProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Gap controls the vertical space between children. Default StackGapMD
	// when zero or unknown.
	Gap StackGap
}

// DefaultStackProps returns sensible defaults: MD gap.
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultStackProps() StackProps {
	return StackProps{
		Gap: StackGapDefault,
	}
}

# ── layout/stylesheet.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

// Stylesheet renders a CSP-safe `<link rel="stylesheet">` tag. Companion to
// Script — ensures consistent, auditable external resource loading. While
// stylesheets are not subject to script-src nonce restrictions, this helper
// provides a single pattern for all external resource tags.
//
// Pass optional attributes (media, crossorigin, integrity) via attrs.
//
//	@layout.Stylesheet("/static/app.css", nil)
//	@layout.Stylesheet("/static/print.css", templ.Attributes{"media": "print"})
templ Stylesheet(href string, attrs templ.Attributes) {
	<link rel="stylesheet" href={ href } { attrs... }/>
}

# ── layout/theme.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package layout

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// ThemeScript renders the inline script that sets the dark mode class before paint.
// Also sets `color-scheme` so native scrollbars, form controls, and <details>
// match the active theme. Include this in your base template head to prevent FOUC.
//
// Only needed for the TOGGLE dark mode strategy (user-controlled .dark class).
// If you use OS-following (prefers-color-scheme), you do NOT need this script —
// Tailwind v4's default dark: variant handles it automatically.
templ ThemeScript(nonce string) {
	if nonce != "" {
		<script nonce={ nonce }>
			(function() {
				var theme;
				try { theme = localStorage.getItem('theme'); } catch(e) {}
				var prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
				var isDark = theme === 'dark' || (!theme && prefersDark);
				if (isDark) {
					document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
				}
				document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
			})();
		</script>
	} else {
		<script>
			(function() {
				var theme;
				try { theme = localStorage.getItem('theme'); } catch(e) {}
				var prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
				var isDark = theme === 'dark' || (!theme && prefersDark);
				if (isDark) {
					document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
				}
				document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
			})();
		</script>
	}
}

// ThemeToggle renders a theme toggle button with sun/moon icons.
// Uses role="switch" + aria-checked so screen-reader users know the active mode.
// Requires Tailwind CSS dark: variants and the ThemeScript in your base layout.
//
// Only needed for the TOGGLE dark mode strategy (user-controlled .dark class).
// If you use OS-following (prefers-color-scheme), dark mode is automatic —
// there is nothing to toggle and this component is unnecessary.
//
//	@layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", nonce)
templ ThemeToggle(ariaLabel string, nonce string) {
	<button
		type="button"
		class={ "rounded-md p-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 hover:text-gray-500 dark:hover:text-gray-300 " + utils.TransitionColors }
		data-theme-toggle
		role="switch"
		aria-checked="false"
		aria-label={ utils.Ternary(ariaLabel != "", ariaLabel, "Toggle theme") }
	>
		@icons.Icon(icons.Moon, "h-5 w-5 dark:hidden")
		@icons.Icon(icons.Sun, "hidden h-5 w-5 dark:block")
	</button>
	if nonce != "" {
		<script nonce={ nonce }>
			(function() {
				var html = document.documentElement;

				function syncToggleAria(btn) {
					if (btn) btn.setAttribute('aria-checked', String(html.classList.contains('dark')));
				}

				// Always sync aria-checked, even after htmx swap re-injects a button
				// with the hardcoded aria-checked="false". This runs on every render;
				// the click listener below is guarded so it only attaches once.
				document.querySelectorAll('[data-theme-toggle]').forEach(syncToggleAria);

				if (!window.tcThemeToggleAttached) {
					window.tcThemeToggleAttached = true;

					document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
					var btn = e.target.closest('[data-theme-toggle]');
					if (!btn) return;
					var isDark = html.classList.contains('dark');
					if (isDark) {
						html.classList.remove('dark');
						try { localStorage.setItem('theme', 'light'); } catch(e) {}
					} else {
						html.classList.add('dark');
						try { localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark'); } catch(e) {}
					}
					html.style.colorScheme = isDark ? 'light' : 'dark';
					document.querySelectorAll('[data-theme-toggle]').forEach(syncToggleAria);
					});
				}
			})();
		</script>
	} else {
		<script>
			(function() {
				var html = document.documentElement;

				function syncToggleAria(btn) {
					if (btn) btn.setAttribute('aria-checked', String(html.classList.contains('dark')));
				}

				// Always sync aria-checked, even after htmx swap re-injects a button
				// with the hardcoded aria-checked="false". This runs on every render;
				// the click listener below is guarded so it only attaches once.
				document.querySelectorAll('[data-theme-toggle]').forEach(syncToggleAria);

				if (!window.tcThemeToggleAttached) {
					window.tcThemeToggleAttached = true;

					document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
					var btn = e.target.closest('[data-theme-toggle]');
					if (!btn) return;
					var isDark = html.classList.contains('dark');
					if (isDark) {
						html.classList.remove('dark');
						try { localStorage.setItem('theme', 'light'); } catch(e) {}
					} else {
						html.classList.add('dark');
						try { localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark'); } catch(e) {}
					}
					html.style.colorScheme = isDark ? 'light' : 'dark';
					document.querySelectorAll('[data-theme-toggle]').forEach(syncToggleAria);
					});
				}
			})();
		</script>
	}
}

# ── navigation/breadcrumbs.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package navigation

import (
	"encoding/json/v2"
	"fmt"
	"net/url"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// BreadcrumbItem represents a single breadcrumb segment
type BreadcrumbItem struct {
	Text   string
	Href   string
	Active bool
}

// BreadcrumbsProps configures a breadcrumb navigation component
type BreadcrumbsProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Items     []BreadcrumbItem
	Separator string
	JSONLD    bool
	// BaseURL is used to resolve relative Hrefs into absolute URLs for
	// JSON-LD structured data (schema.org requires absolute URLs).
	BaseURL string
	// CurrentPath enables auto-detection of the active breadcrumb.
	// When set, the crumb whose Href matches CurrentPath is auto-highlighted.
	// Explicit Active=true on an item always takes priority.
	// When empty, active state falls back to the manual Active flag or
	// an empty Href (terminal crumb).
	CurrentPath string
}

// breadcrumbItemActive determines whether a crumb should render as active.
// Priority: explicit Active flag > empty Href (terminal crumb) > CurrentPath match.
func breadcrumbItemActive(item BreadcrumbItem, currentPath string) bool {
	if item.Active {
		return true
	}
	if item.Href == "" {
		return true
	}
	if currentPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	return IsActive(item.Href, currentPath)
}

// DefaultBreadcrumbsProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultBreadcrumbsProps() BreadcrumbsProps {
	return BreadcrumbsProps{}
}

// breadcrumbJSONLD generates JSON-LD structured data for breadcrumbs.
// Relative Hrefs are resolved against baseURL (schema.org requires absolute URLs).
func breadcrumbJSONLD(items []BreadcrumbItem, baseURL string) string {
	type ListItem struct {
		Type     string `json:"@type"`
		Position int    `json:"position"`
		Name     string `json:"name"`
		Item     string `json:"item,omitempty"`
	}
	type BreadcrumbList struct {
		Context string     `json:"@context"`
		Type    string     `json:"@type"`
		Items   []ListItem `json:"itemListElement"`
	}

	list := BreadcrumbList{
		Context: "https://schema.org",
		Type:    "BreadcrumbList",
		Items:   make([]ListItem, 0, len(items)),
	}
	for i, item := range items {
		entry := ListItem{
			Type:     "ListItem",
			Position: i + 1,
			Name:     item.Text,
		}
		if item.Href != "" {
			entry.Item = resolveBreadcrumbURL(item.Href, baseURL)
		}
		list.Items = append(list.Items, entry)
	}

	data, err := json.Marshal(list)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return string(data)
}

// resolveBreadcrumbURL joins a relative Href to baseURL for JSON-LD output.
// Absolute Hrefs (with a scheme) and protocol-relative URLs (//host) are
// returned unchanged.
func resolveBreadcrumbURL(href, baseURL string) string {
	if href == "" {
		return ""
	}
	parsed, err := url.Parse(href)
	if err != nil || parsed.IsAbs() || strings.HasPrefix(href, "//") {
		return href
	}
	if baseURL == "" {
		return href
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/") + "/" + strings.TrimLeft(href, "/")
}

// breadcrumbSeparator renders the separator between breadcrumb items
templ breadcrumbSeparator(custom string) {
	if custom != "" {
		<span class="mx-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500" aria-hidden="true">{ custom }</span>
	} else {
		@icons.IconRTL(icons.ChevronRight, "h-4 w-4 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500")
	}
}

// Breadcrumbs renders a horizontal breadcrumb navigation
//
//	@navigation.Breadcrumbs(navigation.BreadcrumbsProps{
//	   Items: []navigation.BreadcrumbItem{
//	     {Text: "Home", Href: "/"},
//	     {Text: "Users", Href: "/users"},
//	     {Text: "Edit", Active: true},
//	   },
//	})
templ Breadcrumbs(props BreadcrumbsProps) {
	<nav
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("flex", props.Class) }
		aria-label={ utils.Ternary(props.AriaLabel != "", props.AriaLabel, "Breadcrumb") }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<ol class="inline-flex items-center space-x-1 md:space-x-3">
			for i, item := range props.Items {
				<li class="inline-flex items-center">
					if i > 0 {
						@breadcrumbSeparator(props.Separator)
					}
					@activeSpanOrLink(
						breadcrumbItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath),
						item.Href,
						item.Text,
						"text-sm font-medium text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
						"text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 hover:text-blue-600 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:text-white",
						"",
					)
				</li>
			}
		</ol>
	</nav>
	if props.JSONLD && len(props.Items) > 0 {
		@templ.Raw(fmt.Sprintf(`<script type="application/ld+json">%s</script>`, breadcrumbJSONLD(props.Items, props.BaseURL)))
	}
}

# ── navigation/doc.go ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// Package navigation provides navigation components including navbars, breadcrumbs,
// pagination, and mobile menus.
package navigation

# ── navigation/end_of_list.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package navigation

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// EndOfListProps configures the "no more items" indicator shown at the
// bottom of a list when all items have been loaded (cursor exhausted,
// last page reached, etc.).
type EndOfListProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Message overrides the default "You've reached the end" text.
	Message string
}

// defaultEndOfListMessage is the fallback message when Message is empty.
const defaultEndOfListMessage = "You've reached the end"

// DefaultEndOfListProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultEndOfListProps() EndOfListProps {
	return EndOfListProps{}
}

// EndOfList renders a subtle "no more items" indicator for the bottom of
// a list. Pair it with LoadMore or Pagination to signal that the cursor
// is exhausted or the last page has been reached.
//
//	@navigation.EndOfList(navigation.DefaultEndOfListProps())
//	@navigation.EndOfList(navigation.EndOfListProps{Message: "No more battles"})
templ EndOfList(props EndOfListProps) {
	{{
		message := props.Message
		if message == "" {
			message = defaultEndOfListMessage
		}
	}}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("py-6 text-center text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		role="status"
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ message }
	</div>
}

# ── navigation/loadmore.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package navigation

import (
	"net/url"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// LoadMoreProps configures a "Load more" button for cursor-based pagination.
// The button issues an HTMX request to Endpoint with the current Cursor value.
// The server responds with the next batch of items plus a new LoadMore button
// (with the updated cursor) that replaces this one via hx-swap="outerHTML".
type LoadMoreProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Endpoint is the URL the button requests via hx-get. The cursor is
	// appended as a query parameter (?cursor=...).
	Endpoint string
	// Cursor is the opaque cursor value for the next page of results.
	Cursor string
	// Label is the button text. Defaults to "Load more".
	Label string
	// InfiniteScroll, when true, adds a reveal trigger so the button
	// auto-fires when scrolled into view (infinite scroll pattern). Without
	// Wire this renders htmx's hx-trigger="revealed"; with Wire the typed
	// trigger language renders it in BOTH dialects (ADR-0043): htmx
	// "revealed", Datastar data-on-intersect__once — both fire once on first
	// viewport entry.
	InfiniteScroll bool
	// Wire, when set, re-renders the request wiring in the configured
	// transport (see the utils/wire package, ADR-0036). Wire.URL replaces
	// Endpoint (the cursor is appended to it exactly the same way); swap
	// semantics stay self-replacement via the typed trigger language:
	// under htmx the action renders hx-swap="outerHTML" next to the kept
	// hx-target="this"; under Datastar the fragment replaces this region by
	// id-matching — set ID explicitly so the server can echo the wrapper id
	// back (wire.Handler-style). Wire.Target is ignored (pagination is a GET
	// that replaces itself); Wire.Swap is overridden to outer; an explicit
	// Wire.Event merges with the reveal trigger per ADR-0043.
	Wire *wire.Action
	// FocusOnSwap renders autofocus on the button so the replacement button
	// receives focus after the outerHTML self-swap — verified against the
	// embedded htmx 2.0.10 runtime, which focuses swapped-in [autofocus]
	// elements. Without it the clicked button is REMOVED from the DOM and
	// focus silently drops to <body>, stranding keyboard and screen-reader
	// users mid-list. Set it ONLY on swap-RESPONSE renders (the replacement
	// button); an initial-page button with autofocus would steal focus at
	// document parse. Datastar patching ignores the attribute (dialect note
	// in docs/transport-wiring.md — the Datastar focus story is the LiveRegion).
	FocusOnSwap bool
}

// DefaultLoadMoreProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultLoadMoreProps() LoadMoreProps {
	return LoadMoreProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Label: "Load more",
	}
}

// LoadMore renders a centered "Load more" button for cursor-based pagination.
// The button uses hx-get to fetch the next batch and hx-swap="outerHTML" so the
// server's response (next items + updated LoadMore) replaces this button in
// place. The cursor is appended as a ?cursor= query parameter to the hx-get URL.
//
//	@navigation.LoadMore(navigation.LoadMoreProps{
//	   Endpoint: "/api/items",
//	   Cursor:   nextCursor,
//	})
//
// Pass Wire to switch the dialect while keeping the semantics identical:
//
//	@navigation.LoadMore(navigation.LoadMoreProps{
//	   ID:        "items-load-more",
//	   Wire:      &wire.Action{Transport: wire.TransportDatastar, URL: "/api/items"},
//	   Cursor:    nextCursor,
//	})
templ LoadMore(props LoadMoreProps) {
	{{
		label := props.Label
		if label == "" {
			label = "Load more"
		}
		href := props.Endpoint
		if props.Wire != nil {
			href = props.Wire.URL
		}
		if props.Cursor != "" {
			parsed, err := url.Parse(href)
			if err == nil {
				q := parsed.Query()
				q.Set("cursor", props.Cursor)
				parsed.RawQuery = q.Encode()
				href = parsed.String()
			} else {
				href = href + "?cursor=" + url.QueryEscape(props.Cursor)
			}
		}
		wired := templ.Attributes{}
		isDatastar := false
		if props.Wire != nil {
			a := *props.Wire
			a.URL = href
			a.Target = ""
			a.Swap = wire.PatchModeOuter
			if props.InfiniteScroll {
				a.Reveal = &wire.Reveal{}
			}
			wired = a.Attributes()
			isDatastar = a.Transport == wire.TransportDatastar
		}
	}}
	<div
		id={ utils.EnsureID("load-more", props.ID) }
		class={ utils.Class("flex justify-center py-6", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<button
			type="button"
			{ wired... }
			if props.FocusOnSwap {
				autofocus
			}
			if props.Wire == nil {
				hx-get={ href }
				hx-swap="outerHTML"
				hx-target="this"
				if props.InfiniteScroll {
					hx-trigger="revealed"
				}
		} else {
			if !isDatastar && href != "" {
				hx-target="this"
			}
		}
			class={ "inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 cursor-pointer " + utils.TransitionColors + " focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-blue-400" }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
		>
			{ label }
		</button>
	</div>
}

# ── navigation/mobile_menu.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// mobileMenuToggleClass swaps viewport-keyed (sm:hidden) for container-keyed
// (@sm:hidden) when containerAware is true. Both strings are complete Tailwind
// literals so the content scanner picks them up.
func mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "flex items-center @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "flex items-center sm:hidden"
}

// mobileMenuClass swaps the wrapper's hidden/visible breakpoint the same way.
func mobileMenuClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "hidden sm:hidden"
}

// MobileMenuToggle renders the hamburger button for mobile menus.
// menuID uniquely identifies the menu this toggle controls, so multiple Nav
// instances on one page don't collide on a hardcoded ID.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenuToggle(true, "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenuToggle(show bool, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if show {
		<div class={ mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware) }>
			<button
				type="button"
				class={ "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md p-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:bg-gray-100 hover:text-gray-500 focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-inset focus:ring-blue-500 dark:focus:ring-blue-400 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:text-gray-300 " + utils.TransitionColors }
				aria-controls={ menuID }
				aria-expanded="false"
				data-mobile-menu-toggle={ menuID }
			>
				<span class="sr-only">Open main menu</span>
				@icons.Icon(icons.Menu, "tc-menu-open block h-6 w-6")
				@icons.Icon(icons.X, "tc-menu-close hidden h-6 w-6")
			</button>
		</div>
	}
}

// MobileMenu renders the collapsible mobile navigation menu.
// menuID uniquely identifies this menu; the toggle uses the same ID so the
// aria-controls relationship stays valid even with multiple Navs on a page.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenu(links, "/", "", "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenu(links []NavLinkProps, currentPath string, nonce string, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if len(links) > 0 {
		<div class={ mobileMenuClass(containerAware) } id={ menuID } data-mobile-menu-id={ menuID }>
			<div class="space-y-1 pb-3 pt-2 border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800">
				for _, link := range links {
					@MobileNavLink(link, currentPath)
				}
			</div>
		</div>
		<script { utils.ScriptAttrs(nonce)... }>
			if (!window.tcMobileMenuAttached) {
				window.tcMobileMenuAttached = true;
				function tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, open) {
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var openIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-open');
					var closeIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-close');
					if (!openIcon || !closeIcon) return;
					if (open) {
						menu.classList.remove('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
						var first = menu.querySelector('a[href],button:not([disabled]),input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])');
						if (first) first.focus();
					} else {
						menu.classList.add('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
						btn.focus();
					}
				}
				document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
					var btn = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-toggle]');
					if (!btn) return;
					var menuId = btn.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-toggle');
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var menu = nav.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-id="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!menu) return;
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, menu.classList.contains('hidden'));
				});
				document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
					if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
					var menu = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-id]');
					if (!menu) return;
					if (menu.classList.contains('hidden')) return;
					var menuId = menu.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-id');
					var btn = document.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-toggle="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!btn) return;
					e.preventDefault();
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, false);
				});
			}
		</script>
	}
}

# ── navigation/nav.templ ─────────────────────────────────────────────
package navigation

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// NavProps configures a navigation bar.
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the bar collapse to its hamburger menu
// based on its parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the
// viewport. Useful when Nav is placed inside a sidebar, drawer, or other
// constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
type NavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Brand       templ.Component
	Links       []NavLinkProps
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
	// ContainerAware, when true, wraps the nav in a @container div and swaps
	// sm:/lg: breakpoint classes for @sm:/@lg: so the nav responds to its
	// container width, not the viewport. Default false (viewport breakpoints).
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultNavProps() NavProps {
	return NavProps{
		Sticky: true,
	}
}

// navDesktopLinksClass returns the responsive class for the desktop links
// container, swapping viewport-keyed (sm:) for container-keyed (@sm:) when
// the nav is container-aware. Both strings are complete Tailwind literals.
func navDesktopLinksClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:ms-6 @sm:flex @sm:flex-wrap @sm:gap-x-8 @sm:gap-y-2"
	}
	return "hidden sm:ms-6 sm:flex sm:flex-wrap sm:gap-x-8 sm:gap-y-2"
}

// Nav renders a responsive navigation bar
//
//	@navigation.Nav(navigation.NavProps{
//	   Brand: @myLogo(),
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	     {Href: "/about", Text: "About"},
//	   },
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ Nav(props NavProps) {
	{{ menuID := utils.EnsureID("mobile-menu", props.ID) }}
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@navInner(props, menuID)
		</div>
	} else {
		@navInner(props, menuID)
	}
}

templ navInner(props NavProps, menuID string) {
	<nav
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		aria-label={ utils.Ternary(props.AriaLabel != "", props.AriaLabel, "Main navigation") }
		class={ utils.Class("z-40 border-b border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900", props.Class),
			templ.KV("sticky top-0", props.Sticky) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
			<div class="flex min-h-16 items-center justify-between">
				<div class="flex">
					if props.Brand != nil {
						<div class="flex flex-shrink-0 items-center">
							@props.Brand
						</div>
					}
					<div class={ navDesktopLinksClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
						for _, link := range props.Links {
							@NavLink(link, props.CurrentPath)
						}
					</div>
				</div>
				if props.RightItems != nil {
					<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
						@props.RightItems
					</div>
				}
				@MobileMenuToggle(len(props.Links) > 0, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
			</div>
		</div>
		@MobileMenu(props.Links, props.CurrentPath, props.Nonce, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
	</nav>
}

// SimpleNavProps configures a minimal navigation with a text brand
type SimpleNavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	BrandText string
	BrandHref string
	Links     []NavLinkProps
	// RightItems is rendered on the right side of the bar (e.g. a ThemeToggle,
	// a sign-in button, a user menu). Forwarded to Nav.RightItems. Optional.
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
}

// DefaultSimpleNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSimpleNavProps() SimpleNavProps {
	return SimpleNavProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		BrandHref: "/",
		Sticky:    true,
	}
}

// SimpleNav renders a minimal navigation with text brand
//
//	@navigation.SimpleNav(navigation.SimpleNavProps{
//	   BrandText: "MyApp",
//	   BrandHref: "/",
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	   },
//	   RightItems: @layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", ""),
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ SimpleNav(props SimpleNavProps) {
	@Nav(NavProps{
		BaseProps:   props.GetBaseProps(),
		Brand:       simpleBrand(props.BrandText, props.BrandHref),
		Links:       props.Links,
		RightItems:  props.RightItems,
		CurrentPath: props.CurrentPath,
		Sticky:      props.Sticky,
	})
}

templ simpleBrand(text, href string) {
	<a href={ templ.SafeURL(href) } class="text-xl font-bold text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400">{ text }</a>
}

// FooterLink is one link in a FooterColumn.
type FooterLink struct {
	Text string
	Href string
}

// FooterColumn is a titled group of links in a multi-column footer.
